title: Combination of dasatinib and quercetin promotes osteogenic differentiation and stemness maintenance of hPDLSCs via YAP/TAZ

sections.abstract:
Human periodontal ligament stem cells (hPDLSCs) are candidate seed cells for periodontal tissue regeneration. Enhancing the stemness maintenance and osteogenic differentiation potential of hPDLSCs is conducive to their role in periodontal tissue regeneration. The combination of dasatinib and quercetin, a type of senolytic, has been reported to affect cell senescence. However, whether it can regulate the osteogenic differentiation and stemness maintenance of hPDLSCs, and the related mechanisms, remain unknown. The present study analyzed the optimal concentrations of dasatinib and quercetin in combination for hPDLSCs and found that the combination of dasatinib and quercetin enhanced osteogenic differentiation and promoted the expression of stemness-related markers in hPDLSCs. The expression levels of TAZ and YAP were improved when hPDLSCs were incubated with dasatinib and quercetin. However, the osteogenesis-promoting effects of dasatinib plus quercetin were partly attenuated when TAZ was knocked down, and their effects on stemness-related markers were suppressed when YAP was inhibited. Taken together, the combination of dasatinib and quercetin promotes the osteogenic differentiation and stemness maintenance of hPDLSCs, and YAP/TAZ may be involved in this process. This combination may hold promise for improving hPDLSCs function in periodontal tissue regeneration.

KEYWORDS: Dasatinib, quercetin, hPDLSCs, YAP/TAZ, osteogenic differentiation
sections.introduction:
Periodontitis is a common chronic inflammation characterized by destruction of periodontal supporting tissues. Periodontitis generally lead to the destruction of alveolar bone, which can cause tooth loss (Tay et al. 2025 ). Stem cell-based tissue engineering has put forward new therapeutic strategies for periodontal tissue reconstruction (Zarubova et al. 2022 ; Luo et al. 2023 ; Gao et al. 2024 ). Human periodontal ligament stem cells (hPDLSCs) are important seed cells in periodontal tissue engineering. Their self-renewal capacity and multiple differentiation potential, especially the osteogenic differentiation potential, enable them to proliferate and differentiate into periodontal supporting tissues (Liu et al. 2020 ; Sun et al. 2023 ; An et al. 2024 ). Generally, large amount of seed cells is required for periodontal tissue regeneration. However, the rarity of original cells and the difficulty of large-scale in vitro expansion of cells limits the application of hPDLSCs in tissue engineering, because the loss of stemness and the decrease in osteogenic differentiation ability often occur during in vitro culture (Jiang et al. 2017 ; Ancel et al. 2024 ; Cai et al. 2024 ). Therefore, there is a dire need to improve osteogenic differentiation ability and promote stemness maintenance of hPDLSCs to maximize the therapeutic capacities of them.

The combination of dasatinib and quercetin is a widely studied senolytic drug combination that can selectively clear senescent cells, and thus has been applied in the therapy of a variety of age-related diseases (Khan et al. 2024 ; Ya and Bayraktutan 2024 ; Yao et al. 2024 ; Rattanaprukskul et al. 2025 ). Interestingly, besides inhibiting cell senescence, both dasatinib and quercetin have been reported to have positive effects on other cellular functions, such as promoting osteogenesis (Wang et al. 2023 ; Wang et al. 2024b ). For example, dasatinib accelerates the healing process of bone fracture in mice (Wang et al. 2018 ; Jia et al. 2023 ); quercetin can promote osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow or adipose-derived stem cells (Bian et al. 2021 ; Feng et al. 2023 ; Li et al. 2024 ; Yang et al. 2024 ). Since the osteogenic differentiation and stemness maintenance is quite important for hPDLSC-based bone regeneration, we wonder whether dasatinib plus quercetin treatment have positive effects on these capabilities of hPDLSCs.

TAZ and YAP are transcriptional co-activators in the Hippo signaling pathway, which has been reported to be a key regulator of organ development and tissue homeostasis (Yu et al. 2015 ; Phillips et al. 2024 ). When this pathway is activated, the upstream kinases MST1/2 and LATS1/2 can inhibit the translocation of YAP/TAZ from the cytoplasm to the nucleus, which in turn affects the expression of downstream target genes and subsequently regulates cell activity. As key effectors, TAZ and YAP have been shown to affect the function of several types of stem cells (Robledinos-Anton et al. 2020 ; Meyer et al. 2023 ; Shao et al. 2024 ; Isotani et al. 2025 ). Our previous studies have also demonstrated that TAZ and YAP participate in the regulation of osteogenic differentiation and stemness maintenance in hPDLSCs (Jia et al. 2018 ; Jia et al. 2019 ; Gu et al. 2020 ).

In this study, we examined the effect of dasatinib plus quercetin treatment on the osteogenic differentiation and stemness maintenance of hPDLSCs and explored the possible mechanism. The optimal concentration of dasatinib and the optimal concentration of quercetin for promoting the proliferation and osteogenic differentiation of hPDLSCs were first determined. Then, we investigated the effects of dasatinib plus quercetin treatment on osteogenic differentiation and stemness maintenance of hPDLSCs. To further investigate the possible mechanisms underlying the effects of dasatinib and quercetin combination treatment on the biological functions of hPDLSCs, TAZ knockdown using shRNA and the YAP inhibitor verteporfin were used to preliminarily elucidate the roles of YAP and TAZ during this process.
sections.methods:
The periodontal ligament tissues were obtained from extracted premolars and third molars of healthy donors aged 14–20 and were isolated from the middle 1/3 of the root surface, cut into small pieces, and digested for 1 h in α-minimum Eagle’s medium (α-MEM, Gibco, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA, USA) with collagenase I (3 mg·mL −1 ) and dispase II (4 mg·mL −1 ) at 37°C. Then, dissociated cell suspension was filtered through a 70-μm strainer, and the suspended single cells were plated into petri dishes and cultured in α-MEM medium supplemented with 15% fetal bovine serum (FBS; Gibco, Waltham, MA), 100 U/mL penicillin, and 100 mg/mL streptomycin (Gibco, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA, USA) at 37 °C with 5% CO 2 . BD Stemflow Human MSC Analysis Kit (BD Biosciences, San Jose, CA, USA) was used to detect cell surface markers for stem cells according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

The effects of dasatinib or quercetin on hPDLSCs proliferation were detected by Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8, Dojindo Laboratories, Kumamoto, Japan). Briefly, hPDLSCs were seeded at a density of 3,000 cells per well in 96-well plates with maintenance medium (α-MEM medium with 10% FBS) for 24 h. Afterwards, cells were inoculated with maintenance medium (day 0) containing 0, 0.1, 1, 10, 50, 100, 500 nM dasatinib (Sigma-Aldrich, St. Louis, MO, USA) or 0, 0.5, 1, 2.5, 5, 10 μM quercetin (Sigma-Aldrich, St. Louis, MO, USA). When necessary, vertepofin (Sigma-Aldrich, St. Louis, MO, USA), an inhibitor for YAP (Katayama et al. 2024 ; Luo et al. 2025 ), was added to the culture medium. The cell number was assessed every other day till day 7 using CCK-8 according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

For osteogenic differentiation, hPDLSCs were seeded at a density of 10 5 cells per well in 12-well plates with osteogenic inductive medium, α-MEM supplemented with 10% FBS, 10 nM dexamethasone, 10 mM β-glycero-phosphate, and 50 mg/L ascorbic acid (Solarbio, Beijing, China). Different concentrations of dasatinib or quercetin or a combination of dasatinib and quercetin were added to the medium when necessary. hPDLSCs were cultured in the osteogenic inductive medium for 7 and 21 days, and the medium was changed every 3 days. Then alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity assay, ALP staining, and alizarin red staining were used to analyze the osteogenic differentiation of hPDLSCs. The expression of osteogenic markers was analyzed by western blot.

For adipogenic differentiation, hPDLSCs were seeded at a density of 2 × 10 5 cells per well in 6-well plates with adipogenic inductive medium, α-MEM supplemented with 10% FBS, 0.5 mM 3-isobutyl-1-methylxanthine, 10 μg/mL insulin, 1 μM dexamethasone and 0.2 mM indomethacin (Solarbio, Beijing, China). hPDLSCs were cultured in the adipogenic inductive medium for 28 days, and the medium was changed every 3 days. Oil red O (Solarbio, Beijing, China) was used to detect intracellular lipid droplet formation according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

After 7 days of osteogenic induction, hPDLSCs were scraped into 1% Triton X-100 (Solarbio, Beijing, China). After centrifugation at 12,000 g for 10 min, BCA protein assay kit (Beyotime, Shanghai, China) was used to measure the protein concentration. ALP activity assay was performed using the ALP activity assay kit (Nanjing Jiancheng, Nanjing, China) following the manufacturer’s instructions.

After 7 days of osteogenic induction, hPDLSCs were fixed with 4% paraformaldehyde, and stained with a BCIP/NBT staining kit (Beyotime, Shanghai, China) according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

After 21 days of osteogenic induction, hPDLSCs were fixed with 4% paraformaldehyde, and stained with Alizarin red solution (Solarbio, Beijing, China) for 10 min and observed under a microscope.

hPDLSCs were seeded at a density of 1 × 10 3 cells per well in a 6-well plate and cultured in complete medium for 14 days, after fixation with 4% paraformaldehyde, cells were stained with 0.1% crystal violet solution (Solarbio, Beijing, China) and observed under a microscope.

hPDLSCs were harvested and lysed in RIPA buffer (Solarbio) containing phosphatase inhibitor (Biosharp, Hefei, Anhui, China). Primary antibodies against ALP (Proteintech), RUNX2 (Cell Signaling Technology, Danvers, MA, USA), Collagen I (COL-1, Wanleibio, Shenyang, Liaoning, China), C-MYC (Cell Signaling Technology, Danvers, MA, USA), NANOG (Cell Signaling Technology, Danvers, MA, USA), OCT-4 (Cell Signaling Technology, Danvers, MA, USA), YAP (Cell Signaling Technology, Danvers, MA, USA), TAZ (Cell Signaling Technology, Danvers, MA, USA) and GAPDH (Cell Signaling Technology, Danvers, MA, USA) were diluted and incubated with the membranes overnight at 4℃. Then horseradish peroxidase-conjugated secondary antibody was diluted and incubated with the membranes at room temperature for 1 h. Finally, the membranes were visualized using an ECL Kit (Millipore, Boston, Massachusetts, USA). The intensity of band was quantified using an ImageJ software.

hPDLSCs were seeded at a density of 4 × 10 5 cells per well in 6-well plates and transfected with a PGLV3-h1-GFP-puro vector (GenePharma, Shanghai, China) after cell adhesion, which included a TAZ knockdown (shTAZ) sequence or a negative control sequence (shNC). TAZ knockdown efficacy was evaluated by western blot analysis after 72 h.

Statistical analysis was performed by using student’s t test (comparisons between two groups) and one-way analysis of variance followed by Tukey’s multiple comparisons test (comparisons among three or more groups). Data are displayed as mean ± SEM. P < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
sections.results:
About 1 week after culture, the primary hPDLSCs began to crawl out of the edges of the periodontal ligament tissue, showing a long fusiform (Fig. S1A). Cells from passage 3 to 5 were used in the follow-on experiments (Fig. S1B). Flow cytometry analysis showed that hPDLSCs were positive for mesenchymal stem cell surface markers such as CD29, CD44, CD73, CD90 and were negative for hematopoietic stem cell surface marker such as CD45 ( Figure 1 (A)). To investigate the multi-differentiation capability of hPDLSCs, osteogenic and adipogenic induction were respectively induced. The result showed that ALP staining was positive ( Figure 1 (B)) and mineralized nodules were formed ( Figure 1 (C)) after osteogenic induction, and lipid droplets were formed after adipogenic induction ( Figure 1 (D)). The colony forming assay showed that single hPDLSCs possessed colony-forming activity ( Figure 1 (E)), which indicating a strong self-renewal ability.

Phenotypic characterization detection and drug concentration selection of hPDLSCs. (A) Flow cytometry analysis of the expression level of mesenchymal stem cell surface-specific antigens of hPDLSCs (CD29, CD44, CD73, CD90, CD45). (B) ALP staining of hPDLSCs after osteogenic induction for 7 days. Scale bar = 200 μm. (C) Alizarin red staining of hPDLSCs after osteogenic induction for 21 days. Scale bar = 200 μm. (D) Oil red O staining of hPDLSCs after adipogenic induction for 28 days. Scale bar = 100 μm. (E) Colony forming assay of hPDLSCs. Scale bar = 200 μm. (F)(H) Cell proliferation analysis using the CCK-8 assay when hPDLSCs were incubated with dasatinib(F) and quercetin(H). (G)(I) ALP activity assay of hPDLSCs incubated with dasatinib(G) and quercetin(I). * P < 0.05 versus the concentration of 0 group. ** P < 0.01 versus the concentration of 0 group.

For dasatinib alone, CCK-8 results showed that dasatinib with concentration ≥10 nM inhibited the proliferation of hPDLSCs in a dose-dependent manner at day 5 and day 7 ( Figure 1 (F)). In ALP activity assay, 0.5, 1 nM dasatinib significantly increased ALP activity, while 2, 5, 10 nM dasatinib significantly inhibited ALP activity ( Figure 1 (G)). For quercetin, the viability of hPDLSCs treated with 0.5, 1, 2.5, 5 μM quercetin presented no significant difference compared with the control group, but 10 μM-treated group showed inhibitory effect at day 3 and day 7 compared with the control group ( Figure 1 (H)). After 7 days of osteogenic induction, 0.5, 2.5, 5, 10 μM quercetin treatment significantly improved the ALP activity of hPDLSCs and the 2.5 μM treatment group showed the strongest effect ( Figure 1 (I)). Based on the above results, 1 nM dasatinib alone and 2.5 μM quercetin alone are regarded as the optimal concentrations to improve the ALP activity of hPDLSCs without affecting proliferation.

In order to detect the effects of the combination of dasatinib and quercetin on the osteogenic differentiation of hPDLSCs, we established two groups: a D (1 nM) + Q (2.5 μM) group and a D (10 nM) + Q (2.5 μM) group. This was done because the effects of combining the two drugs may differ from using each drug separately. Therefore, we chose different concentrations of dasatinib and quercetin in the combination, not limited to the optimal concentrations of each drug alone. At the same time, cells without treatment (NC group), cells incubated with 1 nM dasatinib (1 nM D group), and cells incubated with 2.5 μM quercetin (2.5 μM Q group) were used as controls.

After 7 days of osteogenic induction, the results of ALP activity assay and ALP staining showed that both the single drug groups and the combined drug groups had a significant promotive effect on ALP activity. Among them, ALP activity in the combined drug groups were significantly higher than that in the single drug groups, and the ALP activity in the D (10 nM) +Q (2.5 μM) group was significantly higher than that in the D (1 nM) +Q (2.5 μM) group ( Figure 2 (A,C)). Similarly, compared with the NC group, D (1 nM) group, and Q (2.5 μM) group, both the D (10 nM) +Q (2.5 μM) group and the D (1 nM) +Q (2.5 μM) group significantly increased the expression levels of ALP, RUNX2 and COL-1. Interestingly, when comparing the D (10 nM) +Q (2.5 μM) group and the D (1 nM) +Q (2.5 μM) group, the expression level of those proteins in the former was higher than that in latter ( Figure 2 (B)). In alizarin red staining after 21 days of osteogenic induction, the hPDLSCs treated with D (10 nM) +Q (2.5 μM) or D (1 nM) + Q (2.5 μM) deposited more calcium than other treatment groups ( Figure 2 (D)). All the above results imply that the combination of dasatinib and quercetin, especially10 nM dasatinib plus 2.5 μM quercetin, can enhance the osteogenic differentiation of hPDLSCs.

Effect of the combination of dasatinib and quercetin on osteogenic differentiation of hPDLSCs. (A) ALP activity under different treatment groups. (B) Western blot analysis of ALP, RUNX2, COL-1expression in hPDLSCs after osteogenic induction for 7 days. (C) ALP staining of hPDLSCs after osteogenic induction for 7 days. Scale bar = 500 μm. (D) Alizarin red staining of calcium deposition of hPDLSCs after osteogenic induction for 21 days. Scale bar = 250 μm. NC: negative control. Q: quercetin. D: dasatinib. * represents the difference between the intervention group and the NC group, * P < 0.05, ** P < 0.01. # represents the difference between the intervention groups, # P < 0.05, ## P < 0.01.

In periodontal tissue engineering, maintaining the stemness of the transplanted stem cells play an important role in tissue regeneration. In order to detect the influence of the combination of dasatinib and quercetin on stemness maintenance of hPDLSCs, the protein expression levels of stemness-related genes C-MYC, NANOG, OCT-4 were detected by western blot after 3 days of treatment. Since the above experiments showed that the combination of 10 nM dasatinib and 2.5 μM quercetin had the strongest effects on hPDLSCs osteogenesis, this combination was applied in this part of the experiments. The results showed that the expression levels of C-MYC, NANOG and OCT-4 in D (10 nM) +Q (2.5 μM) group were significantly higher than that in the other control groups ( Figure 3 ), which indicates that the combination of dasatinib and quercetin can promote the stemness maintenance of hPDLSCs.

Effect of the combination of dasatinib and quercetin on stemness of hPDLSCs. Western blot analysis of OCT-4, Nanog and C-MYC expression in hPDLSCs after 3 days of treatment. NC: negative control. Q: quercetin. D: dasatinib. * represents the difference between the intervention group and the NC group, ** P < 0.01. # represents the difference between the intervention groups, # P < 0.05, ## P < 0.01.

In order to preliminarily explore whether the mechanism by which dasatinib plus quercetin exerts its effects is related to TAZ and YAP, the protein expression levels of TAZ and YAP in hPDLSCs treated with dasatinib plus quercetin were analyzed by western blot. The results showed that D + Q treatment significantly increased the expression of TAZ and YAP compared with the NC group and the single-drug groups ( Figure 4 (A) and Figure 5 (A)), suggesting that TAZ and YAP may be involved in the regulation by the combination of dasatinib and quercetin.

TAZ knockdown inhibited osteogenic induction of hPDLSCs by the combination of dasatinib and quercetin. (A) Western blot analysis of TAZ expression in hPDLSCs. (B) Western blot analysis of TAZ protein expression after lentivirus transfection. (C) Phase contrast images and fluorescence microscopic images of hPDLSCs after lentivirus transfection. Scale bar = 200 μm. (D) ALP activity under different treatment groups. (E) Western blot analysis of ALP, RUNX2, COL-1 expression in hPDLSCs after osteogenic induction for 7 days. (F) ALP staining of hPDLSCs after osteogenic induction for 7 days. Scale bar = 500 μm. (G) Alizarin red staining of calcium deposition of hPDLSCs after osteogenic induction for 21 days. Scale bar = 250 μm. NC: negative control. Q: quercetin. D: dasatinib. shTAZ: hPDLSCs with TAZ knockdown. shNC: the negative control for shTAZ. * represents the difference between the intervention group and the NC group, ** P < 0.01. # represents the difference between the intervention groups, ## P < 0.01.

YAP inhibitor vertepofin inhibited the effect of the combination of dasatinib and quercetin on hPDLSCs stemness. (A) Western blot analysis of YAP expression in hPDLSCs treated with senolytics. (B) Cell viability analysis of hPDLSCs treated with vertepofin by the CCK-8 assay. (C) Western blot analysis of YAP expression in hPDLSCs treated with vertepofin. (D) Western blot analysis of C-MYC, Nanog and OCT-4 expression in hPDLSCs after 3 days of treatment. NC: negative control. Q: quercetin. D: dasatinib. * represents the difference between the intervention group and the NC group, * P < 0.05, ** P < 0.01. # represents the difference between the intervention groups, # P < 0.05, ## P < 0.01.

To further explore the role of TAZ, we established a lentivirus to knock down the expression of TAZ in hPDLSCs ( Figure 4 (B,C)) and then treated these cells with 10 nM dasatinib plus 2.5 μM quercetin, as before. After osteogenic induction for 7 days, the ALP activity ( Figure 4 (D,F)), the expression levels of osteogenesis-related proteins ( Figure 4 (E)), and the amount of mineralized matrix ( Figure 4 (G)) in the shNC + D + Q group were much higher than those in the shNC group, showing that the combination of dasatinib and quercetin significantly increased the osteogenic differentiation of hPDLSCs. However, those in the shTAZ + D + Q group were lower than those in the shNC + D + Q group, proving that TAZ knockdown reduced the positive effects of dasatinib plus quercetin on osteogenesis ( Figure 4 (D-G)). Therefore, it can be inferred that the combination of dasatinib and quercetin affects the osteogenic differentiation of hPDLSCs partly through TAZ.

Similarly, in order to further explore whether YAP is involved in the effects of senolytics on hPDLSCs stemness, the YAP inhibitor verteporfin, which inhibited YAP expression in a dose-dependent manner ( Figure 5 (B,C)), was added to the culture medium at a concentration of 200 nM. The expression levels of C-MYC, NANOG, and OCT-4 in the D + Q group were higher than those in the NC group ( Figure 5 (D)), which is consistent with previous results showing that D + Q enhances the stemness of hPDLSCs. However, the expression levels of NANOG and OCT-4 in the verteporfin + D + Q group decreased significantly compared with the D + Q group ( Figure 5 (D)), suggesting that the inhibition of YAP reduced the effects of dasatinib plus quercetin on hPDLSCs stemness. Therefore, it can be inferred that the combination of dasatinib and quercetin affects the stemness of hPDLSCs partly through YAP.
sections.discussion:
Senolytics are a class of small molecule drugs that can preventing or treating multiple age-related diseases and alleviating age-related conditions by selectively removing senescent cells (Dungan et al. 2022b ; Suda et al. 2024 ; Zhao et al. 2025 ). The combination of dasatinib and quercetin is a classical type of senolytics drugs, and the research on them involves various aspects such as cell aging (Rattanaprukskul et al. 2025 ), inflammation (Islam et al. 2023 ), and muscle hypertrophy (Dungan et al. 2022a ). However, in addition to selective elimination of senescent cells, the effects of dasatinib and quercetin on other biological characteristics of stem cells are still poorly studied. The present study proved that the combination of dasatinib and quercetin could effectively improve the osteogenic differentiation ability and stemness maintenance of hPDLSCs. As small molecule drugs, dasatinib and quercetin have the advantages of being orally available, not involving immunogenicity, penetrating cell membranes, stable, and easy to store and transport (Nieto et al. 2024 ). Therefore, dasatinib and quercetin have great potential application value in hPDLSCs-based periodontal tissue regeneration.

The osteogenic differentiation ability of hPDLSCs is quite important for the regeneration of periodontal tissue. In this study, we demonstrated that the combination of dasatinib and quercetin promotes the osteogenic differentiation of hPDLSCs, indicating that they can be used as an osteogenic enhancer. Moreover, previous studies have demonstrated that single dasatinib or quercetin promotes the osteogenic differentiation of stem cells (Wang et al. 2018 ; Zhang et al. 2020 ; Bian et al. 2021 ; Zhang et al. 2021 ; Jia et al. 2023 ), while our present results proved that the promotive effects of the combination of dasatinib and quercetin are stronger than those of single drug on osteogenesis. Therefore, the combination treatment of dasatinib and quercetin may be an effective and convenient method for improving hPDLSCs-based bone regeneration. Our results are consistent with some studies that demonstrate the combination of dasatinib and quercetin has positive effects on osteogenesis, even though they draw the conclusion in other types of cells (Zhou et al. 2021 ; Wang et al. 2023 ). However, the present results are limited in in vitro experiments, and more in vivo experiments are required to verify the positive effects of senolytics on the osteogenic differentiation of hPDLSCs.

Large-scale expansion of mesenchymal stem cell with stemness maintenance is essential for cell transplantation, but long-term passage can lead to loss of stemness and decreased expression of stem-related genes (Diomede et al. 2017 ; Jiang et al. 2017 ; Ancel et al. 2024 ; Cai et al. 2024 ). Therefore, it is necessary to develop techniques to maintain stemness of hPDLSCs during in vitro culture. Our study proved that the combination of dasatinib and quercetin treatment could increase the expression levels of C-MYC, NANOG and OCT-4 in hPDLSCs. Since C-MYC, NANOG and OCT-4 are regarded as stemness markers (Wang et al. 2024a ), these results suggest that the combination of dasatinib and quercetin has positive effects on hPDLSCs stemness, so hPDLSCs incubated with the dasatinib plus quercetin may have a better regenerative therapeutic effect in periodontal tissue engineering. Up to now, few studies have reported the potential regulatory effects of the combination of dasatinib and quercetin on the stemness of stem cells. However, our results provide new insights and clues for the multi-functional exploration of these agents.

The mechanism of senolytics regulating stem cell functions has not been fully clarified. Based on several previous studies, the combination of dasatinib and quercetin could regulate the behaviors of cells through various mechanisms, such as regulating NF-κB pathway (Zhao et al. 2025 ), PPARα (Guo et al. 2024 ), and Notch pathway (Zhu et al. 2024 ), while it remains unclear which mechanism is dominant. The present study demonstrated that the combination of dasatinib and quercetin improved the expression levels of TAZ and YAP in hPDLSCs. Since our previous studies have demonstrated that TAZ and YAP play important roles in the regulation of osteogenic differentiation and stemness in hPDLSCs (Jia et al. 2018 , 2019 ; Gu et al. 2020 ), we explored the potential roles of YAP and TAZ in the effects of dasatinib plus quercetin treatment. The results showed that TAZ knockdown or YAP inhibition attenuated the positive effects of dasatinib and quercetin on osteogenic differentiation and stemness maintenance of PDLSCs, thus it can be inferred that YAP/TAZ participate in the regulation of dasatinib and quercetin on hPDLSCs. Notably, few previous studies have reported the potential role of YAP or TAZ in the mechanism of dasatinib and quercetin. One study demonstrated that dasatinib and quercetin could inhibit YAP-1 in osteoarthritic chondrocytes (Maurer et al. 2025 ) which seems to have an opposite conclusion compared to ours. The differences in cell types, drug concentrations, and cell behaviors likely led to the different roles of YAP and TAZ in the function of dasatinib and quercetin, which requires further study. The deficiencies of the present study are that the specific mechanisms of YAP/TAZ signaling in this process are not fully clarified. Nevertheless, the present results provide a foundation for further studies on the mechanisms of dasatinib and quercetin.

To sum up, our study demonstrates that dasatinib plus quercetin treatment can be used as an effective method to promote the osteogenic differentiation and stemness maintenance of hPDLSCs during in vitro culture, and it has good application prospects in periodontal tissue engineering. Additionally, this study is expected to broaden the scope of applications of these agents, along with other senolytic compounds.
sections.conclusion:
The present study demonstrated that the combination of dasatinib and quercetin can regulate the osteogenic differentiation and stemness maintenance of hPDLSCs. The underlying mechanism may be related to YAP/TAZ ( Figure 6 ). Our findings reveal a new role of the combination of dasatinib and quercetin in hPDLSCs, providing novel insights for the application of dasatinib and quercetin in periodontal tissue engineering.

Schematic diagram. The combination of dasatinib and quercetin activated YAP/TAZ, then promoted osteogenic differentiation and stemness maintenance of hPDLSCs.
